definitions.explanation: The spirit of a dead person that appears in the world of the living, often depicted in Japanese tradition as a pale figure with no feet.
Something that exists only in name or on paper, not in reality.

examples.japanese: この{屋敷|やしき}には{幽霊|ゆうれい}が{出|で}るらしい。
examples.english: Apparently ghosts appear in this mansion.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のころ、{幽霊|ゆうれい}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}くと{夜|よる}{眠|ねむ}れなくなった。
examples.english: As a child, when I heard ghost stories I couldn't sleep at night.

examples.japanese: {幽霊|ゆうれい}{会社|かいしゃ}に{注意|ちゅうい}する。
examples.english: To watch out for ghost companies.

examples.japanese: {幽霊|ゆうれい}{会員|かいいん}が{多|おお}すぎる。
examples.english: There are too many phantom members.

examples.japanese: その{団体|だんたい}は{幽霊|ゆうれい}{会員|かいいん}を{除|のぞ}けば{実際|じっさい}の{活動|かつどう}{人数|にんずう}は{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: If you exclude the phantom members, the actual number of active people in the organization is small.

notes:
CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Traditional Japanese {幽霊|ゆうれい} are typically depicted as pale figures wearing white burial kimono ({白装束|しろしょうぞく}), with long disheveled black hair, and characteristically lacking feet. This differs from Western ghosts. Classic examples include {四谷怪談|よつやかいだん} (Yotsuya Ghost Story).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{幽霊|ゆうれい}が{出|で}る (a ghost appears)
・{幽霊|ゆうれい}{屋敷|やしき} (haunted mansion)
・{幽霊|ゆうれい}{会社|かいしゃ} (shell company)
・{幽霊|ゆうれい}{会員|かいいん} (phantom member)
・{幽霊|ゆうれい}{話|ばなし} (ghost story)
